title: Blackwork
summary: Blackwork is black silk worked on white linen: each shape is outlined in a firm stem stitch and filled with a counted geometric pattern of its own, so that trellis, scroll and ring fillings read like fine lace. In Tudor England it trimmed cuffs, collars and caps.
howToPlay: Pick a silk from the skeins and a shape from the tray.
Touch a square on the linen to work that shape there; it is outlined and filled, and mirrored across and down.
Copy the border shown on the pattern sheet, then press Check.
rules: The border is mirrored left to right and top to bottom, so every shape you work is also worked on its partner squares.
A square counts only when its shape and its silk colour both match the border you are copying.
Three stars need a nearly perfect copy; you can undo or clear as often as you like.
heritageNote: Blackwork was fashionable in sixteenth-century England, where it is seen in portraits as the edging of shirts, sleeves and collars; it was often called Spanish work, after the court of Catherine of Aragon. The double running stitch is still known as Holbein stitch.
